question: Does this PR implement the accepted external-verification RFC with an acceptable permanent public plugin API and host-security boundary for protected tool approvals?
rationale: The design direction is recorded as accepted, but this branch makes that direction durable across the plugin SDK, Gateway protocol, native clients, Codex routing, and persisted state; deciding that this exact permanent contract is acceptable requires owner judgment.

options.title: Approve the bounded contract
options.body: Confirm that the host-owned, deny-only generic path and plugin-scoped completion/grant API are the intended permanent extension boundary, then require an exact-head rebase and focused upgrade/security proof.

options.title: Narrow the public seam
options.body: Keep the RFC goal but request a smaller SDK or protocol surface before landing if maintainers do not want the proposed grant-store and verifier API to become supported contracts.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded contract
recommendation.body: Confirm that the host-owned, deny-only generic path and plugin-scoped completion/grant API are the intended permanent extension boundary, then require an exact-head rebase and focused upgrade/security proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The tracker attributes acceptance of the governing RFC design to Kevin, making that decision trail the closest available owner signal.
